newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end weak, Copec rallies.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end weak, Copec rallies.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed slightly lower in thin trade with forestry firm Copec firming on hopes of a rise in world wood pulp prices, said dealers.

The weighted IPSA index ended down 0.07 percent at 131.53 points. The bolsa's negative drift is likely to resume at the opening Friday as investors continue to cash in gains after the recent rally, they said.
"We should see a relatively flat day with the (index) ending around 131 points as a result of profit-taking," said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investments.
The general index shed 0.06 percent at 5,715.8 points in turnover of 10.3 billion pesos.
Copec, Chile's largest cellulose producer, climbed 3.43 percent to 2,110 pesos on optimism that there were signs of a slight improvement in pulp prices, said dealers.

Other gainers included fertilizer-maker Soquimich SQM.SN, which rose on media reports that an Australian lithium producer may stop producing the mineral as it cannot compete with Soquimich's low prices, said traders.
"This is exactly the strategy Soquimich is developing with the majority of its products. It has a great costs advantage," said Tagle.
Soquimich burst onto the world lithium market last year, selling the mineral at 30 percent below world prices.
Soquimich ended up 1.96 percent at 2,600 pesos.

Losers included Banco Santander, down 2.8 percent at 26 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, down 1.3 percent at 227 pesos, and Banco Edwards, which fell 0.93 percent to 53-1/2 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
